title: Tenant-gated policy catalog and audit mappings
body:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a compact, operational reference for tenant-gated IAM policies and the audit mappings required for SIEM ingestion and evidence automation across Redwood’s three hosting modes (hosted, dedicated, private). It focuses on: role definitions, activation workflows, per-environment scoping rules, policy templates, audit-log field mapping for SIEM export, and a short runbook for automating evidence collection for audits.

Design goals (quick):
- Least privilege by default, with just-in-time elevation where needed.
- Clear separation of tenant-level roles (customer-facing) and infra roles (operator).
- Single audit schema that can be normalized by the SIEM regardless of hosting mode.
- Evidence automation (hooks + playbook) that minimizes manual work during compliance requests.

1) High-level role taxonomy (language used across docs)
- tenant_admin: tenant-scoped admin; can manage tenant config, keys, and rollout pins. No infra-level host control.
- tenant_readonly: read-only tenant observer (billing, metrics, logs limited to tenant).
- operator_oncall: infra operator with SRE-run privileges scoped to a cluster/region. Requires MFA and ephemeral activation for write ops.
- operator_lead: long-lived operator role used for deployment/upgrade tasks; limited to dedicated/private control planes.
- auditor_service: service account used to export evidence and run read-only queries against audit stores.
- support_agent: scoped support role for customer support tasks (redacted PII access pattern).

Note: These roles are abstract—policy templates below show how to implement them for each hosting mode.

2) Per-environment scoping rules (short):
- Hosted (multi-tenant):
  - Tenant roles are strongly namespaced: resource names include tenant_id.
  - Operator roles must be restricted to service-level actions only; no cross-tenant reads by default.
  - Any operator write must require ephemeral activation with justification.
- Dedicated (single-tenant but Redwood-managed):
  - Tenant_admin can be mapped to customer-provided admin groups for that capacity reservation.
  - Operator_lead has expanded privileges for node-level maintenance, but must operate under a signed ticket and audit annotation.
- Private (customer-owned control plane / VPC):
  - Redwood operator roles are scoped to maintenance windows and specific customer BYO keys.
  - Where possible, avoid operator write access; use runbooks and signed automation.

3) Example IAM policy templates (JSON snippets — adapt variable placeholders):
- tenant_admin (hosted) sample:
  {
    "Version": "2024-01-01",
    "Statement": [
      {
        "Effect": "Allow",
        "Action": [
          "redwood:TenantRead",
          "redwood:TenantConfigWrite",
          "redwood:ModelPin"
        ],
        "Resource": "arn:redwood:tenant:${tenant_id}:*"
      }
    ]
  }

- operator_oncall (ephemeral activation template):
  {
    "Version": "2024-01-01",
    "Statement": [
      {
        "Effect": "Allow",
        "Action": [
          "redwood:InstanceReboot",
          "redwood:EvictPod",
          "redwood:FlushCache"
        ],
        "Resource": "arn:redwood:infra:region:${region}:*",
        "Condition": {
          "BoolIfExists": {
            "redwood:EphemeralActivation": "true"
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  }

- auditor_service (read-only evidence queries):
  {
    "Version": "2024-01-01",
    "Statement": [
      {
        "Effect": "Allow",
        "Action": [
          "redwood:AuditRead",
          "redwood:LogExport"
        ],
        "Resource": "arn:redwood:audit:workspace:${workspace}:*"
      }
    ]
  }

Implementation notes: replace placeholder variables (${tenant_id}, ${region}) at provisioning time. Keep policy snippets in a shared registry and version them with semantic tags.

4) Audit log schema (single normalized format for SIEM ingestion)
The SIEM pipeline expects a compact, typed JSON per event. Normalize fields across hosted/dedicated/private during export. Key fields used by downstream alerting and evidence automation:
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- event_id (uuid)
- principal_type (user|service|operator)
- principal_id (userid or service-id)
- tenant_id (nullable)
- action (string action name, e.g., TenantConfigWrite)
- resource (ARN-like string)
- outcome (success|failure|partial)
- request_id (trace id correlating to request)
- justification (free text present when ephemeral elevation used)
- evidence_refs (comma-separated artifact ids pointing to snapshots or exports)
- host_context (region/cluster identifier)
- policy_version (policy semantic tag)

SIEM field mappings (how to export):
- log.timestamp -> timestamp
- log.id -> event_id
- auth.principal.type -> principal_type
- auth.principal.id -> principal_id
- context.tenant -> tenant_id
- event.action -> action
- event.resource -> resource
- event.outcome -> outcome
- request.trace -> request_id
- event.meta.justification -> justification
- event.meta.evidence_ids -> evidence_refs
- infra.host -> host_context
- policy.meta.version -> policy_version

Note: keep the mapping file under source control. Use a small normalizer Lambda/worker close to the log store to apply this mapping before pushing to SIEM.

5) Evidence automation runbook (lightweight playbook)
Goal: on-demand assemble minimal evidence set for auditor requests or after a privileged action. Steps: 
- Trigger: either manual audit ticket (JIRA:SEC-xxxx) or automated trigger when an ephemeral activation occurs.
- Step 1: collect event bundle — query the audit store for all events with request_id == activation_request_id and those within +-5 minutes. Export as compressed JSON (gz).
- Step 2: collect config snapshots — pull model pins, tenant settings, and IAM bindings for the tenant and the operator at the time of the action. Store as artifacts with deterministic names: evidence/${request_id}/config.json.
- Step 3: gather host telemetry — reference corresponding infra metrics and node-level logs for the same timeframe. Scrub PII where applicable.
- Step 4: sign and archive — the auditor_service or automation signs the archive with a KMS key and uploads to long-term evidence storage (retention policy applies).
- Step 5: attach artifact ids to the original audit event via event.meta.evidence_ids so SIEM can surface them inline.

Automation tips:
- Use an ephemeral-runner pattern: the evidence collector runs with auditor_service role and only read privileges.
- The collector must annotate each artifact with a provenance block: collected_by, collected_at, collection_query. Store these as simple JSON files inside the archive.
- Include a redact-manifest outlining fields removed for privacy.

6) Example alert rules (SIEM) that depend on this schema:
- Unexpected cross-tenant read: principal_type == "operator" AND action matches ".*Read.*" AND tenant_id != null AND principal_id not in tenant_allowlist => high alert.
- Ephemeral activation without justification: action in (InstanceReboot, EvictPod) AND justification == null => medium alert + auto-ticket create.
- Policy mismatch during rollback: policy_version != latest_catalog_version => create incident for policy drift.

7) Role activation workflow (ephemeral elevation) — short sequence
- Request: operator requests via SelfService UI (web form) with ticket_id and short justification.
- Approval: automated policy checks (oncall roster, blackout windows) run; for high-risk ops human approval required.
- Grant: short-lived tokens issued (TTL 1h default) with redaction controls. Token proof is attached to the audit event as request_id.
- Post-op: operator must mark operation as completed in the ticket; evidence collector auto-runs and attaches artifacts.

8) Example practical extracts and commands (operational conveniences)
- Pull audit bundle for request_id=abc-123 (CLI example):
  curl -sS "https://audit.internal/export?request_id=abc-123" -H "Authorization: Bearer $AUDITOR_TOKEN" | jq . > abc-123-events.json
- Build evidence archive (local):
  tar -czf evidence-abc-123.tgz abc-123-events.json config.json host-logs.json && gpg --sign --armor -u "auditor@redwood.com" evidence-abc-123.tgz

9) Onboarding checklist for new tenants (condensed)
- Ensure tenant_admin group is created and onboarding checklist completed.
- Verify tenant_id namespacing in all resource ARNs.
- Confirm tenant retention and redaction policy is set.
- Configure tenant-specific SIEM tags and routing (if dedicated/private).

10) Open questions / next experiments
- Can we reduce evidence collection time by precomputing per-tenant daily deltas and storing short-lived indexes? (Pros/cons and cost tradeoffs)
- Investigate compact binary event summaries (thrift/protobuf) to speed SIEM throughput and reduce costs.
- Explore integrating KYC gating to support_agent role for regulated tenants (different redaction rules).

Appendix: quick links and references
- IAM catalog repo: github.com/redwood-inference/iam-catalog (tagged templates)
- Audit pipeline design spec: CONFLUENCE:SEC-AUDIT-PIPE-002
- Existing playbooks and runbooks: CONFLUENCE:SEC-PLAYBOOKS

Notes: This doc is intentionally concise — it should act as a single-pane reference to implementers and auditors. For complete policy texts and enforcement code see the iam-catalog repo and the audit pipeline spec linked above.
